# CANDIDATE: MIDDAY_RIBBON_COMPRESSION_BREAKOUT_SHORT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon (8,21,34,55) contracts to its narrowest point of the day, a break below the ribbon signals short‑term mean reversion, offering a short entry. The setup is most effective during midday chop (11:00–13:30 EST) when the market lacks directional conviction, and the volume filter helps avoid false breaks in low‑liquidity periods.

## Mechanism

Calculate ribbon width as (highest EMA − lowest EMA) / price using the 8,21,34,55 EMAs on the 5‑minute chart. Track the lowest width over the last 200 bars. When the current bar’s width equals that 200‑bar minimum **and** the bar closes below the lowest EMA (55 EMA) **and** volume > average volume (20‑bar simple moving average), enter short at the close of that bar. Exit: initial stop placed above the highest EMA (8 EMA) of the ribbon; target set at 1R (risk‑reward 1:1). If the position moves favorably, activate a premium‑stop of 0.5% of entry price to protect any runner. Only consider entries between 11:00–13:30 EST, with VIX between 15‑25, and avoid periods where price shows ≥3 consecutive higher highs or lower lows (strong trend).
